name: Zhang Chunjiao
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, WG Tech (JiangXi) Group Co., Ltd. (沃格光电, SSE: 603773)
profile: Zhang Chunjiao (张春姣, b. Dec 1972) is co-founder of WG Tech, a Xinyu, Jiangxi maker of optoelectronic glass and glass circuit plates founded in 2009 and listed in Shanghai in 2018. Her wealth (per Hurun) is shared with co-founder Yi Weihua, the former controlling shareholder. She became GM in Nov 2022 and chairman in March 2026 after Yi stepped down.
interesting_fact: WG Tech says it is one of very few companies globally with full-process capability for GCP (glass circuit plate) technology, now used for glass-core substrates for high-compute chip packaging, optical-module glass substrates and Mini/MicroLED displays — directly relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company she worked her way through WG Tech as assistant to the general manager, vice president, head of the marketing center and special assistant to the chairman; the company credits her with nearly 20 years in optoelectronic display and supply-chain management.
notes: Name in filings is 张春姣 (input lists 张春娇). Board secretary is Gong Qingyu (龚庆宇); route via board office/IR email. Glass-substrate packaging angle fits the data-center theme.

name: Li Weicheng
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 7-8%) of Raytron Technology (睿创微纳, SSE STAR: 688002); director until the Dec 2025 board re-election
profile: Li Weicheng (李维诚) is an early backer and one of the largest individual shareholders of Raytron Technology, a Yantai, Shandong maker of uncooled infrared thermal-imaging chips founded in 2009 by Ma Hong and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019 among its first batch. He held about 9.2% before selling part of his stake in 2025, and served as a director; he was not named to the board elected in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Raytron, in which he is a top shareholder, designs infrared, microwave and laser sensing chips used in thermal cameras, automotive driver-assist and AI devices; it was among the first 25 companies to list on the STAR Market in July 2019.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal biography found in filings searched. Filings name him and his wife Shi Yun (石筠) as acting-in-concert holders. Not an executive, so the company IR route is indirect. Hurun lists him for 2019-2026.

name: Fu Mingkang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Riyue Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. (日月股份, SSE: 603218)
profile: Fu Mingkang (傅明康, b. 1963), a Ningbo native, founded Riyue Heavy Industry with his wife Chen Jianmin and daughter Fu Linger. The company is a leading maker of heavy-section ductile-iron castings, especially hubs and bases for wind turbines, plus parts for plastics machinery. He started as a technician at a Ningbo elevator factory and still runs Riyue as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Riyue specialises in thick, large-section ductile-iron castings for heavy equipment, a core part of the wind-power supply chain, and runs what it calls a fully digitalised casting plant (the 'new Rixing' digital foundry) in Ningbo.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Riyue, he is a vice president of the China Foundry Association's council, president of the Ningbo Safety Association, and a deputy to the 16th Ningbo Municipal People's Congress; he holds a senior economist title.
notes: Strong energy (wind-power) angle. Board secretary is Lu Jianbo (卢建波). Directly holds about 260.6M shares.

name: Michael F. Petrie
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Merchants Bancorp (Nasdaq: MBIN), Carmel, Indiana; Chairman of Merchants Bank of Indiana
profile: Michael Petrie co-founded Merchants Capital Corp., a multifamily and healthcare mortgage lender, with Randall Rogers in August 1990. It grew into Merchants Bancorp, an Indiana bank holding company focused on multifamily and affordable-housing finance that listed on Nasdaq in 2017. He has been chairman and CEO since 2006, and his large insider stake underpins his wealth.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he chaired the Mortgage Bankers Association's Board of Directors in Washington, D.C., and he has more than 40 years in mortgage banking.
deep_cut_fact: An Indiana University lifer (BS and MBA in finance), he serves on the IU Varsity Club's National Board and the advisory board of IU's Center for Real Estate Studies. He is also a trustee of the Michael F. Petrie & Jody J. Petrie Foundation and a director of the Indianapolis Neighborhood Housing Partnership.
notes: Contacts are from the Feb 19, 2026 press release (investor contact Tami Durle, media contact Rebecca Marsh). Affordable-housing finance angle; quoted regularly in quarterly results.

name: Lan Huasheng
current_role: Chairman and general manager of Shenzhen Dasheng Agriculture Group (深圳市大生农业集团), per older filings; current role unverified
profile: Lan Huasheng (兰华升) controls Shenzhen Dasheng Agriculture Group, an agricultural commodities, fertilizer and agri-finance group. From June 2014 he chaired its Hong Kong-listed arm, Dasheng Agriculture Finance (01103.HK). Dasheng lost its controlling stake in mid-2018 after the CEFC China Energy (Huaxin) crisis hit the group, and the HK company was later delisted. He was on Hurun's lists from 2015 to 2019.
interesting_fact: Lan held 70% of Qianhai Dasheng, making him the de facto controller of Shenzhen Dasheng, the group that built an agriculture-plus-finance platform in Hong Kong in the mid-2010s.
notes: Dropped off rich lists after 2019. The listed vehicle is delisted and the group had financial difficulties after 2018, so his net worth figure is likely stale. No current public contact route found. Low priority.
